text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- Security police chief Seppo Nevala says espionage by foreign countries has increased in Finland, but that Finnish police are on top of the situation.
- Alcohol-related deaths have increased sharply, with as many people dying of drink last year as in road accidents.
- Crime inspired by racial hatred is on the rise in Finland, though slowly, interior ministry says.
- Hundred-year-old Partek seeking to sharpen its profile as a diversified group, though diversification no longer in style.
KAUPPALEHTI
- State-owned oil company Neste Oy exploring ways to limit its speculative oil trading losses by extracting itself from existing contracts.
- Finns beginning to get interested in Russian shares, but Finnish brokers have no Russian stock funds to offer.
- Electronics giant Semi-Tech Global plans to boost television set output at Turku plant acquired from Nokia.
- Skandia's new chief Lars-Eric Petersson says consolidation is needed in the Nordic insurance industry.
DEMARI
- Social Democratic Party secretary-general rejects Centre and Conservative parties' ideas on work reform -- says reform would "poison" the labour market.
- Sixteen Finnish ice hockey players may play in the NHL this season.
AAMULEHTI
- Finnish nurses want health-care institutions to establish ethical guidelines.
- German Member of European Parliament Willi Gorlach says increasingly critical European paper consumers greater threat to Finnish forest industry than EU forestry policy.
TURUN SANOMAT
- Speaker of Parliament Riitta Uosukainen said women still subject to more stringent social scrutiny than men -- said fight for equality far from over.
- Young Finns' party, with just two seats in Parliament, hopes to double its electoral support in Finland's October 20 European Parliament election.
